midnight_rule: Hour 24 closes the narrative day; the world calendar has advanced to the next day.

broadcasts.title: Morning weather
broadcasts.text: Good morning. Elliot Ward here, North Ridge Public Radio at six. A cold start, with changeable cloud later. The clinic is open; Nurse Roy is covering house calls this morning. Regular deliveries are expected. Logging crews, keep the junction clear for the fuel truck. City trains are running normally. Another bulletin at noon.

broadcasts.title: Midday recap
broadcasts.text: It is noon. Elliot Ward with the morning recap: cold weather, normal deliveries, and the clinic open for essential care. Nurse Roy asks callers to check in before entering the treatment room. Logging-road crews should leave the junction clear. The city rail service is operating. Our next bulletin is at five.

broadcasts.title: Distant incidents
broadcasts.text: Elliot Ward with the five o'clock report. Hospitals and transit stations on the other side of the country are reporting violent incidents. Officials have not linked them. There are no confirmed North Ridge cases. City rail departures continue, though some stations are closing early. We will verify what we can before midnight.

broadcasts.title: First overnight update
broadcasts.text: It is midnight. Elliot Ward, still at North Ridge. Several cities now report violent attacks. Hospitals are restricting access, and some emergency crews are not answering. Intercity trains have been suspended. Officials still dispute the cause. No local evacuation order has been issued. Keep your radio available. We will return at six.

broadcasts.title: Regional precautions
broadcasts.text: Good morning. Elliot Ward here. Overnight disturbances have reached our region. Nurse Roy has moved clinic screening to the rear service yard; keep its exit clear. Police advise avoiding crowds and unnecessary travel. Deliveries may be delayed. The city rail service remains suspended. Keep essential supplies at home. A recap at noon.

broadcasts.title: Regional midday recap
broadcasts.text: It is noon. This morning's advice remains: avoid crowds and unnecessary travel. The clinic is screening in its rear yard; do not enter without checking the notice. Hospitals report violent behaviour, and the cause remains unconfirmed. City trains are still suspended. North Ridge deliveries are delayed. Further confirmed information at five.

broadcasts.title: Town disruption
broadcasts.text: This is the five o'clock bulletin. There have been attacks on responders near the North Ridge clinic and the western town junction. Several roads into town are closed. Shops are shutting early and fuel deliveries have been suspended. Stay clear of the clinic and roadblocks. This station is checking reports with the remaining emergency crews.

broadcasts.title: Unexplained deaths
broadcasts.text: It is midnight. Responders describe people moving again after injuries they believed were fatal. Those accounts have not been independently verified, but the attacks are real. The clinic cannot accept further patients. Residents should remain indoors where possible, secure entrances, and prepare drinking water, food and heating fuel. Our next scheduled report is at six.

broadcasts.title: Shelter advisory
broadcasts.text: Good morning. Multiple emergency teams now confirm that some of the dead are rising and attacking the living. Avoid close contact with anyone showing aggressive or disoriented behaviour. North Ridge residents should shelter where they can. Electrical service is becoming unreliable across the region. Fill clean containers with water and keep a safe source of heat ready.

broadcasts.title: Shelter midday recap
broadcasts.text: It is noon. This morning's advice remains in force: avoid close contact with the infected, secure your shelter, and prepare water, food and heating fuel. Reports of the dead rising have been confirmed by several emergency teams. Electrical failures are spreading. A repaired local installation cannot restore the regional network. Travel only when your supplies require it.

broadcasts.title: Northern isolation
broadcasts.text: Elliot Ward with the five o'clock bulletin. Nurse Roy's final message says the clinic staff left on foot after transport failed. Do not wait there for a vehicle. Assistance cannot reach the logging roads. Choose your return route before travelling. This transmitter has reserve power, but our outside contacts are becoming scarce.

broadcasts.title: No relief convoy
broadcasts.text: It is midnight. No relief convoy has reached North Ridge. Several communities are no longer answering radio checks. Do not leave a defensible shelter simply because you expect collection. Treat water, protect wounds and conserve medical supplies. We will continue the scheduled bulletins while this station can operate. The next is at six.

broadcasts.title: Independent survival
broadcasts.text: Good morning. There is no reliable regional power or emergency service. Overnight reports place infected groups on roads into and through town. Keep enough fuel to stay warm after dark. If you must seek supplies, plan your return before setting out. This station cannot promise rescue. Our noon bulletin will repeat the practical advice we can still verify.

broadcasts.title: Independent survival recap
broadcasts.text: It is noon. A recap of this morning's advice: assume help and regular deliveries are unavailable. Maintain your shelter, treat drinking water, and keep dry heating fuel in reserve. Infected groups have been reported along the town approaches. Travel with a return route and leave room to carry useful supplies. Do not spend your final reserves waiting for rescue.

broadcasts.title: Shrinking information
broadcasts.text: This is the five o'clock bulletin. We have fewer working contacts and cannot verify the condition of every road. Silence from a community does not mean that it is safe. Store doors, clinic grounds and traffic queues remain dangerous places to linger. There will be no scheduled supply deliveries. Concentrate on water, warmth and a defensible place to rest.

broadcasts.title: Station reserve warning
broadcasts.text: It is midnight. Elliot Ward. We are on reserve power. I kept the regular times because someone might still be waiting for a familiar voice. There are no dependable services behind these bulletins. Keep your local equipment working. A voice is not a promise of rescue. We will try again at six.

broadcasts.title: Final operating day
broadcasts.text: Good morning from North Ridge. This is expected to be our final day of scheduled broadcasting. Our reserve power is nearly exhausted. There is still no confirmed relief operation for the northern communities. Maintain water, warmth and food before considering another journey. We intend to return at noon, five, and midnight if the transmitter holds.

broadcasts.title: Final midday recap
broadcasts.text: It is noon. This morning's notice remains unchanged: today is expected to be the final operating day for this station. No relief service has been confirmed. Conserve medical supplies, keep drinking water safe, and prepare your shelter for another cold night. We intend to make the five o'clock report and a final midnight signoff.

broadcasts.title: Preparing for silence
broadcasts.text: This is the five o'clock bulletin. We have no new verified outside reports. The transmitter has enough reserve for the planned midnight signoff. Do not treat the silence afterwards as an all clear. Continue the precautions you already know. Keep a route home, keep dry fuel, and help the people you can reach without abandoning your own shelter.

broadcasts.title: Final signoff
broadcasts.text: It is midnight. Elliot Ward, North Ridge Public Radio. This is our final scheduled transmission. No bulletin will follow at six. The names on our call sheet are still here, even when nobody answers. Keep your shelter secure, your water clean and your people warm. You have already survived without dependable help. North Ridge signing off.

broadcasts.title: Assignment check
broadcasts.text: Kestrel Seven, June at dispatch. Good signal. Inspect the transfer cabinet; your replacement relay is reserved at North Ridge Supply. Mara left timber markers and a crew cache on the access track. Check the labelled feeder before isolating it. The lookout is yours for the week. Read the desk log before travelling.

broadcasts.title: Afternoon work check
broadcasts.text: Kestrel Seven, June. Mara says the crew cache has drinking water and dressings. It is a reserve, not tomorrow's delivery. The replacement relay is at North Ridge Supply. Take the logging track and leave daylight for the climb back. Your handset monitors public news too. Put it in its charger between trips.

broadcasts.title: End of shift
broadcasts.text: Kestrel Seven, June's last check tonight. Mara made it back to the junction. We heard the distant reports, but your assignment still stands. Stay at the lookout. Feed the stove and charge the handset. If somebody in the city is not answering, try again tomorrow. We will check in at eight.

broadcasts.title: Travel precautions
broadcasts.text: Kestrel Seven, June. This has reached our region. Mara is taking the town crew towards the clinic service yard; the waiting room is crowded. Keep clear unless supplies force a visit. Collect your reserved relay if it is safe, then come home. Take the handset and leave enough daylight for the stairs.

broadcasts.title: Delivery cancelled
broadcasts.text: Kestrel Seven, June. The supply truck is cancelled. Do not wait beside the road. Mara asked me to tell you the marked cache is yours if you need it. Nothing more is being sent. Keep the lookout as your base. Commission the relay if you can, but water and heating fuel come first.

broadcasts.title: Town crew missing
broadcasts.text: Kestrel Seven, June. Mara's last call was from the western junction. Then the town crew stopped answering. Do not go searching without water and a way home. I know you have people in the city. We cannot get a message through there either. Secure the lookout. I will try you in the morning.

broadcasts.title: Working independently
broadcasts.text: Kestrel Seven, June. We cannot send anyone. Nurse Roy left a notice at the clinic; supplies are still on its shelves, but do not expect staff. Your installation only supports local equipment. Repairing it will not restore the town. Keep water, heating fuel and food in reserve. Listen for public reports when you can.

broadcasts.title: Conserve local power
broadcasts.text: Kestrel Seven, June. If mains have failed, switch off lights you do not need. Isolating the labelled crew spur reduces standby drain. Charge the handset while local power lasts. Mara has not answered. I am leaving her channel open, but you should not spend your last reserves waiting with me. Shelter and water first.

broadcasts.title: Dispatch thinning out
broadcasts.text: Kestrel Seven, June. There are very few names answering now. Keep treating water and securing your shelter. Town stock will not be replenished. Choose the return route before leaving, and leave room in your pack. I will try one more morning check. You do not need to finish the assignment to deserve a rest.

broadcasts.title: Last dispatch call
broadcasts.text: Kestrel Seven. June. I cannot maintain this net. You are released from the assignment. Use the lookout and the tools to keep yourself alive. The public station is independent; it may still be broadcasting. If Mara reaches you, tell her I stayed as long as I could. Do not wait for us. Dispatch out.

characters.family: Elise, your sister in the city
